items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq5y: Ukraine's President Zelensky said US intelligence sharing on Russian missile strikes is working again after talks with Trump envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo, following Kyiv's earlier claim that Washington had withheld intel. items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2: A US judge sentenced Guatemalan national Rigoberto Ramon Miranda-Orozco to 30 years in prison for his role in a 2022 human-smuggling operation in which 53 migrants died trapped in a truck near San Antonio, Texas. He was extradited from Guatemala in 2025. The case highlights the deadly risks of smuggling networks moving migrants across the US-Mexico border.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o: Nigeria confirmed an Ebola case in Abuja after a woman who had transited through Uganda tested positive; she had actually been on a business trip to Congo, where exposure likely occurred. Health officials are tracing 44 contacts to contain it. The case raises concern about Ebola spreading into West Africa's most populous nation.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq0m: France is split over who caused the violent riots that followed student protests on October 17, with looting seen as opportunistic but the broader unrest viewed by some as possibly pre-planned. No clear culprit has emerged, and theories vary on who benefits. The disagreement reflects deeper divisions over trust in institutions and competing political narratives.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2: Jean Claude Hategekimana, a former fighter with Congo-based Rwandan rebel group FDLR, returned to Rwanda and entered a demobilization program after his unit was defeated near Goma. FDLR leaders had warned members that returning home meant death, but he found this false. His story reflects a wider trend of fighters leaving the group amid recent military setbacks in eastern Congo.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o: Police in Guinea-Bissau raided the offices of vaccine researchers praised by US health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, seizing hepatitis B vaccine doses linked to a disputed newborn study funded by $3.2 million from the US CDC and two foundations. Officials said the seizure doesn't indicate the vaccines are unsafe, but it deepens scrutiny of the already contested trial.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmly: Elon Musk said a merger between Tesla and SpaceX, his two biggest companies, is under active consideration, with special committees at both firms examining the idea. No terms have been agreed and shareholder approval would be needed. Tesla is valued near $1.5 trillion and SpaceX at $2 trillion, so combining them would create one of the largest corporate mergers ever.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2: A year after opposition leader Raila Odinga's death, his party ODM is split over whether to cooperate with President William Ruto's government, highlighted by the removal of a secretary-general who opposed closer ties. The rift raises doubts about whether Kenya's opposition can stay unified without the figure who long defined it.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026: The US Department of Homeland Security said roughly 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese will keep temporary protected status, which had been set to expire, though it gave no timeline for a final decision. The move is a temporary reprieve from the Trump administration, which has generally sought to end such protections for migrants.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c678: A 43-year-old man, named locally as activist Brendan Nugent, has been charged after Australian MP Helen Haines was hit by a car in Victoria and left in critical condition after losing a leg. He faces charges including dangerous driving causing serious injury and harming a public official, and will appear in court.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/d: Delhi Traffic Police issued an advisory restricting six roads in Dwarka for a few hours on October 20 evening due to heavy crowds expected for Dussehra, including the burning of a 221-foot Ravana effigy, one of India's tallest. The group said they were exercising their right to protest like burning a Ravana effigy, but police stopped the demonstration.

One suspect, Kunal, allegedly collected the pistol and ammunition from Amritsar. Police have not confirmed the weapon's direct link to the shooting.

items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/m: At Shiv Sena (UBT)'s 60th Dussehra rally in Mumbai, led by Uddhav Thackeray, supporters raised concerns about rising crime—citing incidents like the Tiger Shroff shooting—alongside farmers' distress, unemployment and inflation. items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Delhi Police's Special Cell arrested four more suspects—Kunal, Sumit, Radha and Babita—for allegedly supplying weapons used in the October 18 shooting at Tiger Shroff's car, then handed them to Mumbai Police's CID. Survey data shows finance is a clear second mover, with 48% of finance workers asked to use AI chatbots, offering other industries a blueprint for how adoption unfolds.

Meta says it's reviewing how to prevent such links from being found while reconsidering the sharing feature's design.
items.https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/10/: Ukraine's military used a six-rotor drone to evacuate a wounded soldier from a frontline area too dangerous for ground vehicles due to Russian drones and landmines, marking a real-world test of a long-discussed battlefield evacuation concept. Officials called it a historic step toward systematic drone-based casualty evacuation as the war drives rapid military-technology innovation.

items.https://www.theverge.com/science/1013954: The US is building more fossil fuel power infrastructure than in the past decade, even as renewable growth slows and electricity demand climbs faster than it has in years, driven by data centers, factories and EVs, a new report finds. The Trump administration has favored fossil fuels over wind and solar, risking higher costs and pollution for decades if pending gas projects proceed.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/20/anthro: Anthropic is reportedly shopping a draft federal AI safety bill to Congress that would let regulators block a model's release only with a judge's permission, in cases posing an imminent risk of over 50 deaths or $1 billion in damage from a bioweapon, loss of developer control, or cyberattack. Critics say its framing limits regulators more than it restricts AI.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: A US judge dismissed, with prejudice, Ann Altman's lawsuit alleging her brother, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, sexually abused her as a child, meaning it cannot be refiled. The judge cited her failure to attend a required medical exam and meet other deadlines. Altman's family has denied the allegations; the court also denied Sam Altman's request for attorney fees.

items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/20/openai: OpenAI acquired four-year-old biotech startup Orchestra Bio, whose AI agents help drug-discovery companies manage finances and clinical-trial scheduling, to bolster its Rosalind life-sciences AI model and Rosalind Workbench research tool.
